objective: The guide is read, not operated: an agent resuming, or a human asking what is waiting on them, opens AGENTS.md, then badf/current-state.json, then badf/next-actions.json, then the tracker, and assembles the answer by hand every time. control/index.html assembles it once - the resume decision, the active Work Package, the validator's step-8 reconciliation, the actions waiting on a human, the authority keys grouped by the domain each names, the validator's own check list and provenance for every one of them - generated at build time into the staged artifact and committed as an empty placeholder (#352).
completed: control/index.html is the 29th tracked page - `git ls-files '*.html' | wc -l` moved 28 to 29 - and carries an empty, clearly-marked placeholder in every one of its seven data regions. Each placeholder says the page has not been generated AND names the command that generates it; a test reads every region and asserts both phrases, and two controls trip it.

scripts/build_control_page.py projects badf/current-state.json, badf/next-actions.json and whatever scripts/validate_continuity.py prints into `<!--BTG-CONTROL:name-->` regions. It runs with no arguments to write control/index.html in place so a person can look at it, and with --out to write elsewhere. The markers survive injection, so re-running it against its own output re-projects rather than appends.

NOTHING GENERATED IS COMMITTED. .github/workflows/pages.yml gains one step, after 'Stage immutable site artifact' and before both verification steps, running `python3 scripts/build_control_page.py --out _site/control/index.html`. The staging step's `git ls-files '*.html'` glob has already copied the placeholder there; the projector OVERWRITES that one file, creating none and deleting none, so 'Verify every tracked page reached the artifact' still finds every page. Simulated locally step for step: 29 staged pages before and after, both verifications exit 0, and the tracked file still carried its seven placeholder notices with git status clean.

THE RECONCILIATION IS NOT REIMPLEMENTED. The projector INVOKES scripts/validate_continuity.py and parses its stdout, so WP-112's step 8 has one implementation and the integrity panel is the validator's own PASS/ERROR lines rather than a second check list. A test reads every subprocess argument list in the projector and asserts its first element is `git` or `sys.executable`; nothing else is run and no network module is imported.

AN AUTHORITY KEY THAT NAMES NO DOMAIN RENDERS UNDER Unscoped. The rule is derived and printed on the page in its own words: the key's first underscore-separated segment is the domain it names, and a single-segment key names none. Live, that puts `implementation` under Unscoped and `production_platform_implementation` under `production`, which is #346 and open. A lookup table would have had to place `implementation` somewhere, and placing it IS the guess #346 is about; a control adds exactly such a table and shows the test go red.

AN ABSENT RECORD IS UNKNOWN, NOT AN EMPTY PANEL - the round-1 repair. Measured at d38040a by deleting badf/next-actions.json from a copy and running the projector: the queue panel rendered 'No recorded action matches the filter. That is a reading of badf/next-actions.json' - false, because nothing had been read - then 'The 0 recorded action(s) the filter did NOT admit' and 'The filter excluded no recorded action', exit 0. read_json had always returned a reason and both call sites in build() discarded it with `current, _ = read_json(...)`, while the module docstring promised 'UNKNOWN with the reason beside it'. The reason is now threaded build -> gather -> render_unknown, every panel fed by a record that can be absent renders UNKNOWN with it, and the count, the excluded list and the explanatory sentences are suppressed rather than drawn with zeroes. Re-measured on the same copy: 'badf/next-actions.json could not be read: FileNotFoundError. Nothing else is shown in this panel.'

A DOCUMENT THAT LOADED AND CARRIES NO `actions` ARRAY IS THE THIRD CASE and is UNKNOWN too, because the file was read and still says nothing about the queue. A record that WAS read and is genuinely empty keeps the empty-queue wording, and a test asserts that distinction in both directions - it is the whole point of the repair.

tests/test_control_page.py holds the placeholder, the derivations and the wiring in 66 tests, subprocess-free. scripts/build_control_page.py is split for it: observe() runs git and the validator, gather() is pure, and every test hands gather() a synthetic observation.

scripts/wp113_controls.py runs 35 controls on fresh COPIES, the unmutated copy first and green: 30 mutations each trip the test named for them, one is a declared hole expecting the suite to stay GREEN, and four run the projector itself in two pairs - a copy that is not a repository, and a copy with badf/next-actions.json deleted - each pair's second member removing the guard that makes the first member's answer what it is.

380 tests OK, skipped=1 (314 measured on main at 67deeb2, 66 in this module); validate_continuity.py CONTINUITY_VALIDATION=PASS with html-pages:29; scripts/wp113_controls.py 35 controls, 0 not behaving as declared.
remaining: The Google Fonts link on control/index.html, as on all 29 pages. The brief ordered the shared skeleton copied including it; the coordinator ruled that #352's 'no network call' sits beside 'no tracker synchronisation, no GitHub call' and targets data and tracker requests, and filed the question separately rather than fixing it here. Removing it from one page alone would make that page inconsistent with the site.

Everything else in BIZTRUST-GUIDE-DYN-001: the 25-item navigation, the phase and epic projections, the agent queue, the evidence explorer and the drift dashboard. Each is worth doing and none is needed to prove this surface, which is what DYN-001 section 52 asked for.
#302 (one status vocabulary or three axes) and #307 (the completion matrix, which waits on #302) both stay open, and the page renders no percentage and invents no status word until they are answered.
#346 is rendered rather than repaired. Fixing the key is a records edit and an operator's; this page exists partly to show the defect.

validation.command: python scripts/wp113_controls.py (35 controls on fresh copies, unmutated copy first, one expecting GREEN)

observations: THE ONE REAL DEFECT OF ROUND 1 WAS AGAIN A SENTENCE THAT DID NOT MATCH A MEASUREMENT, and it was a sentence the CODE wrote. With badf/next-actions.json absent the queue panel printed 'That is a reading of badf/next-actions.json, not a statement that nothing is waiting' - and nothing had been read. The counts beside it were zeroes, which look like measurements and were not. #352 says the projector emits UNKNOWN where a fact is absent and never a convenient value; an empty rendering IS a convenient value, and that is the sentence the repair is built from.

THE REASON EXISTED THE WHOLE TIME AND WAS THROWN AWAY AT THE CALL SITE. read_json returned (document, reason) from the first commit; build() read `current, _ = read_json(...)` twice. The projector's own docstring promised the absent case would render 'UNKNOWN with the reason beside it', so the module carried a written claim that nothing in it could satisfy. A discarded return value is a claim's quietest failure mode: nothing is wrong at the point of the discard, and the false sentence is seventy lines away.

A TEST CAN BE SATISFIED BY THE SENTENCE UNDERNEATH THE THING IT IS ABOUT. test_a_missing_record_renders_unknown_in_every_panel_without_raising asserted UNKNOWN over each panel's whole rendering. Every panel ends with a shared provenance line, and that line says UNKNOWN for the source commit of any tree git cannot read - so the assertion passed for the queue panel while its body was drawing an empty table over a file it had never opened. The repair splits the provenance sentence off and asserts over the body, and a control now reduces the UNKNOWN panel to its provenance line and shows the test go red. The lesson generalises: when every panel shares a footer, an assertion over the whole panel is an assertion about the footer.

unittest LETS SystemExit OUT OF THE RUNNER, AND THREE CONTROLS FOUND IT AT ONCE. inject() raised SystemExit on a template/projector mismatch. Three mutations - a builder removed, a region added, the decision region moved - each produced exit 1 with NOT ONE named failure and no summary at all, so the control runner could not say what had caught them. It now raises ProjectionError, an ordinary exception, and main() converts it; a test asserts the class is not a SystemExit subclass. A library function that raises SystemExit is a library function whose failures no test framework can attribute.

MOVING A MARKED REGION IS NOT THE SAME AS NESTING ONE. The control that moves the decision region below the package region first inserted it BEFORE the package region's closing marker, which nested the decision markers inside the package region; the non-greedy pattern then found no decision region at all, and the control tripped a different defect from the one it was named for. It inserts after the closing marker now. A control that reproduces the wrong condition is worse than no control, because it reports PASS.

ROLLING THIS RECORD FORWARD WAS AUDITED BEFORE IT WAS DONE, because WP-112 lost three of nineteen controls to exactly that. Three fragilities were found and repaired. The control that writes a record value into the committed placeholder had the literal WAIT_FOR_AUTHORITY in it while the test it aims at compares against whatever the record spells; it now reads the value from badf/current-state.json. test_the_excluded_actions_are_listed_with_their_authority iterates the excluded list and would have passed while measuring nothing if the filter ever admitted every action; a positive control now asserts both lists are non-empty. And the #346 assertion is now paired with test_every_recorded_key_lands_where_the_rule_puts_it, which re-derives the RULE over whatever keys the record holds and cannot go red for a records edit. See declared_non_coverage for the one dependence deliberately kept.

THE ROLL-FORWARD MOVES THE RECONCILIATION FROM LAG_EXPECTED TO CONSISTENT, measured rather than predicted: WP-113 is recorded active, has not landed, and the recorded baseline 67deeb2 is main's tip. tests/test_resume_reconciliation.py - WP-112's live test, rewritten in its round 3 to stop pinning a package name - stayed green across the change, which is the first time that repair has been exercised by a package other than its own.

MY BRIEF DID NOT ASK FOR badf/ RE-ANCHORING AND AGENTS.MD SECTION 6 REQUIRES IT ANYWAY. It was flagged as a concern rather than done, which was right - a record edit on an agent's own initiative is how records drift - and the coordinator corrected the scope. The general form is worth keeping: where a brief and a standing rule disagree, say so in the report and do not resolve it alone.

A HEREDOC IS NOT A SAFE WAY TO PASS PYTHON CONTAINING BACKSLASHES ON THIS PLATFORM. Two scripted patches silently failed to match strings that were byte-identical in the file, because backslash sequences in the heredoc did not survive the shell. Both were re-done by writing the patch to a file and running it. The rule: never pass code with escapes through a heredoc here; write it to a file first.

A REGENERATED control/index.html IN THE WORKING TREE TURNS THE SUITE RED BY DESIGN, and one of the nine failures is a trap. See recovery.stop_if's last entry and the docstring of scripts/build_control_page.py before repairing anything: the fix is `git checkout -- control/index.html`, not an edit to tests/test_html_adr_citations.py.
assumptions: That the first underscore-separated segment of an authority key names the domain that key governs. This is a SPELLING rule, not a semantic one - `resume_decision_taxonomy` groups under `resume` because that is its first segment, not because anything says the key governs resumption. What the rule actually guarantees is the narrow thing #346 asked for: a key that names NO domain is never placed under a guessed one. If a key ever names its domain in a later segment, it groups wrongly and nothing here would say so.

That an action waits on a human when its recorded `authority` contains HUMAN or WAIT, or its recorded `owner_role` contains `human`. Those are substrings of strings the record already spells, so the filter renames nothing, and the page prints the rule and lists every action it EXCLUDED with that action's authority string so the count can be checked rather than trusted. An action that waits on a person while spelling neither token is missed.

That `git ls-files '*.html'` in the workflow's staging step is what carries control/index.html into the artifact, so the projection can overwrite one staged file rather than create one. A test asserts that glob is still in the workflow; if the staging step ever stopped copying tracked HTML, the verification step would still find _site/control/index.html - written by the projection - and pass while every other page was missing.

That the validator's stdout format - CONTINUITY_VALIDATION=, PASS: name:value, ERROR:, and the four single-value lines - is stable enough to parse. The four single-value lines are read BY NAME rather than by position, because their order is the validator's to change; the check list is read positionally only in the sense that it is rendered in the order printed.

authority.scope_note: One published page is added, one build-time projector, one test module, one control runner, and one workflow step. No existing page is edited, no stylesheet is changed, no record value is re-worded and no gate is recorded. The page grants nothing and records nothing.

recovery.first_safe_command: python -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_control_page.py'   # and if the suite is already red, run `git status` before anything else: a regenerated control/index.html in the working tree turns it red by design, and `git checkout -- control/index.html` is the whole fix
stop_if: A generated value is committed into control/index.html. The tracked file is a placeholder and a test compares every region against the record's own resume_decision, package id, primary action id, baseline commit and updated_at; a file that is true when written and false thereafter is the defect class #343, #345, #346 and #347 all describe.
The projector is made to write into the tracked tree from the workflow. It writes into _site/ and only into _site/; the tracked page must stay a placeholder on every CI run.

An absent, unreadable or malformed record is rendered as an empty panel, a zero or a blank value. UNKNOWN with the reason is the answer. This WAS the behaviour at d38040a and it is the one criterion of #352 the page failed.

A status word is invented, or a recorded value is re-worded on the page. state, authority and resume_decision are rendered exactly as the records spell them; whether the guide should carry separate status axes is #302, open and an operator's.
authority.implementation is 'fixed' so that the Unscoped group empties. That key is defect #346, it is open, and the page exists partly to show it. Repairing it is a records edit and an operator's.
A write control - Authorize, Accept, Record Gate, Close - or any form, button or script is added to the page. It links to where a decision is recorded; it never records one.
The page begins reading the tracker, at build time or in the browser. #311 is the open decision about whether anything should, and the projector runs git and the validator and nothing else.
A completion percentage is put on the page without its denominator and its metric beside it. #307, the completion matrix, waits on #302.
The map issues' tickets are listed. The page may link a map; #301 is open on whether maps stay issues at all.

A limit or a rendered sentence is edited without a control or a command that measures it. Every finding across thirteen review rounds on this repository was a sentence that did not match a measurement; name the command before writing the sentence.

control/index.html is added to CITING_PAGES in tests/test_html_adr_citations.py, or that module is otherwise edited to accommodate the generated page. MEASURED: running `python scripts/build_control_page.py` in a working tree and then the suite gives NINE failures - seven subtests of test_every_committed_region_says_it_is_not_generated, one per region, plus test_no_committed_region_carries_a_value_read_from_a_record, which are the placeholder ratchet firing exactly as intended, and then test_the_same_pages_cite_adrs, because NS-041 and NS-042's recorded prose names ADR-001 to ADR-020 and the projector renders that prose verbatim, so the generated page joins the ADR-citing set. THE FIX IS `git checkout -- control/index.html`; all nine then go green. Registering the page instead is the wrong repair and fails in the opposite direction the moment the placeholder is restored or CI checks out a fresh tree, because CITING_PAGES is an exact set equality and the committed page is a placeholder that cites nothing. Whether the page cites an ADR is a property of the RECORDS at the moment of generation, not of the tracked file, so there is nothing about it a registry can hold.

declared_non_coverage: THE PROJECTOR'S IMPURE HALF IS NEVER RUN BY tests/. observe() - the git calls and the validator invocation - read_json, and build() are all outside the suite, because tests/test_control_page.py runs no subprocess and that property is worth keeping - a module that shells out can go red for an environment reason. NOT because tests/ as a whole is subprocess-free: four modules there call one (test_resume_reconciliation.py, test_resume_schema_identity.py, test_validator_fails_closed.py and test_wp024_fixtures_are_sealed.py), measured with `grep -lnE "subprocess[.](run|Popen|check_output|check_call)" tests/*.py`, and an earlier wording of this entry named two of the four. Grepping for the word rather than the call returns six. A defect confined to those functions is invisible to the suite. It is covered instead by the four SCRIPT controls in scripts/wp113_controls.py, which run the projector in a fresh copy, and by the workflow step, which fails the build if the projector cannot run. A control demonstrates the hole rather than this sentence asserting it: it changes `git rev-parse HEAD` to `--short HEAD`, so the provenance panel would publish a 7-character abbreviation under a label reading 'source commit', and it expects the suite to stay GREEN. If it ever goes red the hole has closed and this entry must be re-derived, not deleted.

ONE TEST DEPENDS ON THE RECORD ON PURPOSE, AND SAYS SO. test_the_live_unscoped_key_is_exactly_the_one_346_names asserts that badf/current-state.json still carries `implementation` unscoped beside `production_platform_implementation`. It is a ratchet on #346 being live, which is why the page carries a callout about it, and test_the_unscoped_group_is_named_on_the_page rests on the same premise. If #346 is repaired in the record both go red, and the repair is to delete them together with the page's Unscoped callout - NOT to weaken test_every_recorded_key_lands_where_the_rule_puts_it, which re-derives the rule over whatever keys the record holds and is record-independent.

THE PAGE'S APPEARANCE IS NOT TESTED. That the .next-action panel renders with its amber border, that the decision is legible, that the tables scroll on a phone - all of it is a review responsibility. What is tested is that the decision is the FIRST projected region and that the recorded word appears inside a heading in it. RESUME_DECISION is nonetheless not the first thing in <main>: the page's static framing precedes it - a section heading, a lede, two intro paragraphs, an .invariant, a .callout, then the decision section's own h2 and intro - which is 352 visible words, measured by stripping tags from the source between <main id="main"> and the decision marker and counting whitespace-separated tokens. That framing is what makes the panel readable and is not projected data; nothing tests how it looks.

NOTHING HERE ASSERTS THAT A RECORD VALUE IS CORRECT. The page copies what the records spell; if badf/current-state.json records the wrong Work Package the suite is green and the page is wrong, faithfully. Reconciling the record against observed git is scripts/validate_continuity.py's step 8 and tests/test_resume_reconciliation.py's, and the reconciliation panel renders that verdict rather than a second one.

THE HUMAN-QUEUE FILTER IS HELD TO ITS OWN WORDING AND NOT TO A JUDGEMENT ABOUT WHO IS REALLY BLOCKED. An action that waits on a person while its authority spells neither HUMAN nor WAIT and whose owner_role spells no human is missed. The mitigation is on the page rather than in the suite: the filter is printed, and every excluded action is listed with the authority string it carries.

THE COMPLETION-PERCENTAGE GUARD IS THE ABSENCE OF ANY `%` FROM THE PAGE. That is broader than the prohibition - a legitimate `%` in a record value would fail it - and narrower in another direction, since a percentage written in words would pass. It is the cheapest reading that cannot be satisfied by relabelling, and the test's docstring says so. If a record ever carries a `%`, that test is where the decision gets made rather than where it is silently lost.

THE MAP-INDEX GUARD READS ONLY THE PAGE'S OWN PROSE. It looks for a run of three or more bare issue references outside a link, in the static source with every injected region removed. The records' own prose quotes such runs - NS-041 names #102 to #125 - and that prose is projected verbatim, so the guard cannot be applied to it without failing on the record rather than on the page. The page therefore relies on the records not becoming an index, which nothing checks.

THE GOOGLE FONTS LINK IS A NETWORK REQUEST AND IS NOT FORBIDDEN HERE. Every page in this guide loads it and the brief ordered the skeleton copied including it. The coordinator ruled that #352's 'no network call' targets data and tracker requests, and filed the question separately; what the assertions here forbid is a script, a fetch or a tracker call inside a projected region. Removing the link from all 29 pages is a separate change with its own review.

TWELVE OF THE THIRTY RED CONTROLS ARE NOT ISOLATED, and the runner prints what else each one trips. The largest is 'the UNKNOWN panel reduced to its provenance line', which trips four tests by design: it is the mutation that shows the round-1 repair holds, and every test about an absent record reads the panel body it empties.

scripts/wp113_controls.py IS NOT WIRED INTO CI, deliberately: every control copies the whole tree, and the four script controls then run the validator inside that copy. Its results are evidence about the tree at the commit someone last ran it against, not a standing guarantee. Nothing detects it rotting, and the script says so in its own docstring.

THE PROJECTOR ADDS A SECOND VALIDATOR RUN TO EVERY CI BUILD. The workflow already runs scripts/validate_continuity.py in its own step and the projector runs it again to read its output. That is the price of the integrity panel being the validator's own list rather than a reimplementation; the alternative, teeing the earlier step's stdout to a file, couples two workflow steps by a filename and was not done pre-emptively. No performance budget is asserted for it.
